questions.question: Which tissue is responsible for movement in our body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscular tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Muscular tissue is responsible for the movement of the body and its parts.
 
• There are three types of muscular tissue: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle.
 
• Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and cause voluntary movements.
 
• Cardiac muscle tissue is found only in the heart and is responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Smooth muscle tissue is found in walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels and is responsible for involuntary movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nervous tissue**

 
 
• Nervous tissue is responsible for transmitting nerve impulses and is found in the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.
 
• It plays a crucial role in controlling and coordinating body activities.
 
 
 
• **Epithelial tissue**
 
 
• Epithelial tissue forms the lining of internal and external surfaces of the body, including skin and the lining of organs.
 
• It provides protection and is involved in absorption, secretion, and sensation.
 
 
 
• **Connective tissue**
 
 
• Connective tissue supports, binds, and protects other tissues and organs.
 
• It includes bone, cartilage, adipose tissue, and blood.

questions.question: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is +0.75. The image is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect and diminished**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is given as +0.75.
 
• A positive magnification indicates that the image is virtual and erect.
 
• The magnification value (0.75) is less than 1, indicating that the image is diminished.
 
• Virtual images formed by spherical mirrors are always erect.
 
• Therefore, the image is virtual, erect, and diminished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirrors**

 
 
• Concave mirrors can produce both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object.
 
• When the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror, a virtual, erect, and enlarged image is formed.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• Convex mirrors always produce virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.
 
• These mirrors are commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Magnification Formula**
 
 
• The magnification (m) produced by a spherical mirror is given by the formula m = -v/u, where v is the image distance and u is the object distance.
 
• A positive value of magnification indicates a virtual and erect image, while a negative value indicates a real and inverted image.

questions.question: Consider a parallel combination of 2 resistors with resistances 4 Ω and 6 Ω. The equivalent resistance of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2.4Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When resistors are connected in a **parallel combination**, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula for the equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is:

 **1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂**, where R₁ and R₂ are the resistances of the individual resistors.
 
• Here, the given resistances are **4Ω** and **6Ω**.
 
• Substitute the values into the formula:

 **1/R_eq = 1/4 + 1/6**.
 
• Find the least common denominator (LCD) of 4 and 6, which is **12**. Rewrite the fractions:

 **1/R_eq = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12**.
 
• Reciprocate the result to find the equivalent resistance:

 **R_eq = 12/5 = 2.4Ω**.
 
• Thus, the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is **2.4Ω**.
 
• Parallel circuits are commonly used in **electrical systems** to ensure that the voltage across each component is the same and to reduce the overall resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **4.2Ω**__

 __
 
• This value might be mistaken as the result if the formula for parallel resistance is applied incorrectly or if the calculation is done improperly.
 
 
 
• **10Ω**__
 __
 
• This value corresponds to the sum of the resistances **(4Ω + 6Ω)**, which is the formula for resistances in series, not parallel. This is incorrect in the context of the given question.
 
 
 
• **12Ω**__
 
 
• This value might confuse learners who think that one of the resistances directly represents the equivalent resistance, but it is not applicable in a parallel circuit.

questions.question: All liquids and gases are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fluids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• All liquids and gases are considered **fluids** because they can flow.
 
• Fluids do not have a fixed shape and they take the shape of their container.
 
• Unlike solids, fluids have the ability to deform continuously under an applied shear stress.
 
• The molecules in fluids are not as tightly packed as in solids, allowing them to move freely past one another.
 
• Fluids can be characterized by their viscosity, which is a measure of their resistance to flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solids**

 
 
• Solids have a definite shape and volume because their molecules are tightly packed and only vibrate in place.
 
• They do not flow like fluids and are rigid in nature.
 
 
 
• **Semiconductors**
 
 
• Semiconductors are materials that have a conductivity between conductors (metals) and insulators (non-metals).
 
• They are used in electronic devices to control the flow of current.
 
 
 
• **Insulators**
 
 
• Insulators are materials that do not allow the flow of electric current easily.
 
• They are used to protect us from the harmful effects of electricity by preventing unwanted flow of current.

questions.question: What type of reaction takes place when a single reactant breaks down into simpler products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• It generally requires an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity to break the chemical bonds.
 
• Decomposition reactions are the opposite of combination reactions, where simpler substances combine to form a more complex compound.
 
• Examples of decomposition reactions include the breakdown of water into hydrogen and oxygen and the breakdown of calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.
 
• These reactions are important in various industrial processes and in the decomposition of organic matter in natural environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination Reaction**

 
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
 
• Example: The reaction of hydrogen and oxygen to form water.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• In a displacement reaction, one element replaces another element in a compound.
 
• Example: The reaction of zinc with hydrochloric acid to produce zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• In a double displacement reaction, the ions of two compounds exchange places in an aqueous solution to form two new compounds.
 
• Example: The reaction of sodium sulfate with barium chloride to form barium sulfate and sodium chloride.

questions.question: Identify the single cell organism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amoeba** is a single-celled organism commonly found in freshwater environments.
 
• It belongs to the **protist kingdom** and is known for its ability to change shape due to its flexible cell membrane.
 
• Amoebas move by extending their **pseudopodia** (false feet), which are temporary projections of the cell.
 
• They feed through a process called **phagocytosis**, where they engulf food particles with their pseudopodia.
 
• Amoebas reproduce asexually through a process called **binary fission**, where the cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seaweed**

 
 
• Seaweeds are multicellular marine algae and are not single-celled organisms.
 
• They play a crucial role in marine ecosystems, providing food and habitat for marine life.
 
 
 
• **Leech**
 
 
• Leeches are multicellular parasitic or predatory worms belonging to the phylum Annelida.
 
• They are known for their bloodsucking behavior and are used in medical treatments for bloodletting.
 
 
 
• **Liver fluke**
 
 
• Liver flukes are parasitic flatworms belonging to the class Trematoda.
 
• They infect the liver and bile ducts of various mammals, including humans.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of particles of matter?

options.text: Particles of matter have space between them.
Particles of matter are continuously moving.
Particles of matter attract each other.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles of matter are static.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Particles of matter are always in a state of continuous motion, hence they are not static.
 
• Particles of matter have spaces between them, which allows them to move and interact.
 
• The movement of particles is influenced by temperature; higher temperatures increase their kinetic energy and motion.
 
• Particles of matter attract each other due to intermolecular forces, which can vary in strength depending on the type of matter.
 
• The concept of matter being static contradicts the kinetic theory of matter which states that particles are always in motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **States of Matter**

 
 
• Matter exists in different states: solid, liquid, and gas, each with distinct characteristics based on particle arrangement and movement.
 
• In solids, particles are closely packed and have limited movement. In liquids, they are less tightly packed and move more freely. In gases, particles move rapidly and are far apart.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Theory of Matter**
 
 
• This theory explains that matter is made up of particles which are in constant motion.
 
• The energy of particles increases with temperature, affecting their state and behavior.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces**
 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion between particles of matter.
 
• They play a crucial role in determining the physical properties of substances, such as boiling and melting points.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the ratio by mass of hydrogen to oxygen atoms (H:O) in a water molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1:8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A water molecule (H₂O) consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• The atomic mass of hydrogen is approximately 1 u (atomic mass unit), and the atomic mass of oxygen is approximately 16 u.
 
• Therefore, the total mass of the hydrogen atoms in a water molecule is 2 u (2 hydrogen atoms × 1 u).
 
• The mass of the oxygen atom in a water molecule is 16 u.
 
• The ratio by mass of hydrogen to oxygen atoms in a water molecule is thus 2:16, which simplifies to 1:8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Molecule Structure**

 
 
• Water is a polar molecule, with the oxygen atom having a partial negative charge and the hydrogen atoms having partial positive charges.
 
• This polarity leads to hydrogen bonding between water molecules, which gives water its unique properties such as high surface tension and boiling point.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonding**
 
 
• Hydrogen bonds are weak bonds that form between the hydrogen atom of one water molecule and the oxygen atom of another water molecule.
 
• These bonds are responsible for many of water's unusual properties, including its high specific heat capacity and its role as a universal solvent.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Water**
 
 
• Water is essential for life, serving as a solvent, a temperature buffer, and a reactant in various biochemical processes.
 
• It is also used in numerous industrial applications, including cooling, cleaning, and as a raw material in chemical reactions.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is responsible for the survival of species over time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Variation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Variation is crucial for the survival of species as it provides a pool of different traits that can be beneficial in changing environments.
 
• Genetic variation increases the likelihood that some individuals in a population will possess traits suited to new or altered conditions.
 
• Natural selection acts on variations within a population, leading to the survival and reproduction of individuals with advantageous traits.
 
• Over time, these advantageous traits become more common in the population, aiding in the species' adaptation and survival.
 
• Without variation, a species may not be able to adapt to environmental changes, leading to extinction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conservation**

 
 
• Conservation involves protecting and preserving natural resources and the environment.
 
• It helps in maintaining biodiversity and preventing the extinction of species.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction**
 
 
• Reproduction is the biological process by which new individual organisms are produced.
 
• It ensures the continuation of species but does not alone guarantee the survival of species over time.
 
 
 
• **Struggle for Existence**
 
 
• The struggle for existence refers to the competition between individuals of a species for limited resources.
 
• It is a driving force in natural selection, leading to the survival of the fittest.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines around a straight current carrying conductor look like:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**concentric circles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor form **concentric circles**.
 
• The direction of these magnetic field lines can be determined using the **Right-Hand Rule**.
 
• As the distance from the conductor increases, the spacing between the concentric circles increases, indicating that the magnetic field strength decreases.
 
• The magnetic field lines are **perpendicular** to the current-carrying conductor.
 
• This phenomenon is described by **Ampere's Circuital Law**, which relates the magnetic field around a conductor to the current passing through it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field**

 
 
• A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• Magnetic fields are produced by electric currents, which can be macroscopic currents in wires, or microscopic currents associated with electrons in atomic orbits.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetism**
 
 
• Electromagnetism is a branch of physics involving the study of the electromagnetic force, a type of physical interaction that occurs between electrically charged particles.
 
• It encompasses various phenomena such as electricity, magnetism, and light.
 
 
 
• **Faraday's Law of Induction**
 
 
• Faraday's Law states that a change in the magnetic field within a closed loop induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the wire.
 
• This principle is the working mechanism behind electric generators and transformers.

questions.question: Regarding carbon, which of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon is tetravalent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms.
 
• This tetravalent nature of carbon is fundamental to the chemistry of life, as it enables the formation of complex molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.
 
• Carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds, increasing the diversity and complexity of carbon-based compounds.
 
• The ability to form long carbon chains and rings is unique to carbon, making it the backbone of organic chemistry.
 
• Carbon's tetravalency allows it to bond with various elements, including hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur, further expanding the range of possible organic molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**

 
 
• Carbon exists in several allotropes, including diamond, graphite, graphene, and fullerenes, each with distinct properties.
 
• In diamond, carbon atoms are arranged in a tetrahedral lattice, making it extremely hard.
 
• In graphite, carbon atoms are arranged in layers of hexagonal lattices, making it a good conductor of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Cycle**
 
 
• The carbon cycle is the process by which carbon moves through the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere.
 
• It plays a crucial role in regulating Earth's climate and supporting life by recycling carbon dioxide and organic carbon.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dating**
 
 
• Carbon dating, or radiocarbon dating, is a method used to determine the age of ancient artifacts and fossils.
 
• It is based on the decay of carbon-14, a radioactive isotope of carbon, to nitrogen-14 over time.

questions.question: When white light falls on a glass prism, it splits into seven colours. The phenomena is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dispersion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dispersion is the phenomenon where white light splits into its constituent colors when it passes through a prism.
 
• This occurs because different colors of light bend by different amounts when they pass through the prism.
 
• The seven colors observed are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
 
• The angle of deviation is different for each color, leading to the separation of colors.
 
• Dispersion is a result of the variation of the refractive index of the material with the wavelength of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffraction**

 
 
• Diffraction is the bending of light waves around obstacles and openings.
 
• This phenomenon is more pronounced when the size of the obstacle or opening is comparable to the wavelength of light.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with different densities.
 
• This change in direction occurs due to a change in the speed of light in different media.
 
 
 
• **Deviation**
 
 
• Deviation refers to the change in direction of light when it passes through a prism or other optical device.
 
• The angle of deviation depends on the angle of incidence and the refractive index of the material.

questions.question: Milk is a mixture of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**water, fat, protein, etc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Milk is a complex mixture containing water, proteins, fats, lactose, minerals, and vitamins.
 
• The main protein in milk is casein, which constitutes about 80% of the protein content in cow's milk.
 
• Milk fat is present in the form of emulsified globules and is a significant source of energy.
 
• Lactose, also known as milk sugar, is the primary carbohydrate found in milk.
 
• Minerals like calcium and phosphorus are abundant in milk, making it essential for bone health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein Types in Milk**

 
 
• Casein and whey are the two primary types of proteins found in milk.
 
• Whey protein is a by-product of cheese production and is often used in protein supplements.
 
 
 
• **Milk Processing**
 
 
• Milk undergoes various processing steps like pasteurization to ensure it is safe for consumption.
 
• Homogenization is another process that breaks down fat molecules so that they remain integrated rather than separating as cream.
 
 
 
• **Milk Varieties**
 
 
• There are different types of milk available such as whole milk, skim milk, and lactose-free milk.
 
• Each type caters to specific dietary needs and preferences.

questions.question:
Select the correct sentence(s).

a. The release of energy in the aerobic process is a lot greater than in the anaerobic process.

b. ATP is broken down giving rise to a fixed amount of energy which can drive the endothermic reactions taking place in the cell.

c. The pyruvate is converted into lactic acid which is also a three-carbon molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The release of energy in the aerobic process is significantly greater than in the anaerobic process.
 
• ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is broken down to release a fixed amount of energy which can drive the endothermic reactions taking place in the cell.
 
• Pyruvate, a three-carbon molecule, is converted into lactic acid, which is also a three-carbon molecule during anaerobic respiration.
 
• In aerobic respiration, glucose is fully oxidized to carbon dioxide and water, producing a high yield of ATP.
 
• Anaerobic respiration is less efficient and results in the production of less ATP and byproducts like lactic acid or ethanol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellular Respiration**

 
 
• This is a set of metabolic reactions and processes that take place in the cells of organisms to convert biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP.
 
• It involves both aerobic and anaerobic pathways depending on the presence of oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Glycolysis**
 
 
• It is the first step in both aerobic and anaerobic respiration, taking place in the cytoplasm of the cell.
 
• Glycolysis breaks down glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, yielding a net gain of two ATP molecules.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**
 
 
• It is an anaerobic process by which cells generate energy through the conversion of glucose to lactic acid or ethanol.
 
• Fermentation allows cells to produce ATP without oxygen, though it is much less efficient compared to aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Name the scientist who first discovered the cell in 1665.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Robert Hooke was the first scientist to discover cells in 1665.
 
• He made this discovery while observing a thin slice of cork under a microscope.
 
• Hooke coined the term "cell" because the cork cells reminded him of the cells (small rooms) in a monastery.
 
• This discovery was published in his book "Micrographia".
 
• Hooke's work laid the foundation for the development of cell theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Matthias Jakob Schleiden**

 
 
• He was a German botanist who co-founded the cell theory.
 
• Schleiden proposed that all plants are made of cells.
 
 
 
• **Theodor Schwann**
 
 
• He was a German physiologist who also co-founded the cell theory.
 
• Schwann extended the cell theory to animals, proposing that all living things are composed of cells.
 
 
 
• **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek**
 
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of Microbiology".
 
• Van Leeuwenhoek was the first to observe and describe single-celled organisms (protozoa and bacteria) using a microscope.

questions.question: What determines the chemical properties of a carbon compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Functional group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The functional group in a carbon compound is primarily responsible for its chemical properties.
 
• Functional groups are specific groups of atoms within molecules that have their own characteristic properties, regardless of the other atoms present in a molecule.
 
• Examples of functional groups include hydroxyl groups (-OH), carboxyl groups (-COOH), and amino groups (-NH₂).
 
• The reactivity of a carbon compound can be significantly altered by the presence of different functional groups.
 
• Functional groups are key determinants in the chemical reactions that a molecule can undergo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Mass**

 
 
• Molecular mass is the sum of the masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
• It influences the physical properties of a substance, such as boiling and melting points, but not the chemical properties directly.
 
 
 
• **Number of Hydrogen Atoms**
 
 
• The number of hydrogen atoms in a carbon compound can affect its saturation level, but is not a primary determinant of its chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **Length of the Carbon Chain**
 
 
• The length of the carbon chain can influence the physical properties of the compound, such as solubility and boiling point, but the functional group is more critical in determining chemical reactivity.

questions.question: What happens when pea plants showing two different characteristics (the tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait), rather than just one are bred with each other?

options.text: The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.
They are all tall and have round seeds in F2 generation.
Some F1 progeny are tall plants with round seeds, and some are short plants with wrinkled seeds.
The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are dependently inherited.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When pea plants showing two different characteristics are bred, each trait is inherited independently of the other.
 
• This observation is consistent with Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, which states that alleles of different genes assort independently of one another during gamete formation.
 
• The F1 progeny will all be heterozygous, exhibiting the dominant traits for both characteristics.
 
• In the F2 generation, a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio is typically observed, showing independent assortment.
 
• This means that the combination of traits can vary, resulting in plants that may be tall with round seeds, tall with wrinkled seeds, short with round seeds, or short with wrinkled seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Segregation**

 
 
• Mendel's first law states that the two alleles for a heritable character segregate (separate) during gamete formation and end up in different gametes.
 
• This law ensures that offspring acquire one allele from each parent for each trait.
 
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**
 
 
• According to this law, in a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic.
 
• The dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype, while the recessive allele is masked in the presence of the dominant allele.
 
 
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**
 
 
• A cross between individuals focusing on a single trait, which illustrates the inheritance of one characteristic.
 
• It typically results in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5.
When pH of rain water is less than 5.6, it is called acid rain.
Living organisms can survive only in a narrow range of pH change.
When pH of rain water is more than 5.6, it is called acid rain.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5. This is because acidic conditions can erode the enamel on teeth.
 
• When the pH of rainwater is less than 5.6, it is referred to as acid rain. This occurs due to the presence of sulfuric and nitric acids in the atmosphere.
 
• Living organisms can survive only in a narrow range of pH change, as extreme pH levels can disrupt biological processes.
 
• When the pH of rainwater is more than 5.6, it is not considered acid rain. Therefore, option 4 is incorrect.
 
• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral. Below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic (alkaline).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acid Rain**

 
 
• Acid rain can have harmful effects on plants, aquatic animals, and infrastructure.
 
• It is primarily caused by emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) which react with water molecules in the atmosphere to produce acids.
 
 
 
• **pH in Human Body**
 
 
• The human body maintains a tightly regulated pH level in the blood, typically around 7.4, which is slightly alkaline.
 
• Enzymatic activities within the body are highly sensitive to changes in pH.
 
 
 
• **Buffer Solutions**
 
 
• Buffer solutions are used to maintain a stable pH in a system, even when small amounts of acid or base are added.
 
• They are essential in many biochemical and industrial processes.

questions.question: When a motorcar makes a sharp turn at a high speed, we tend to get thrown to one side. This example is based on which law of motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tendency to get thrown to one side when a motorcar makes a sharp turn at high speed is explained by **Newton's First Law of Motion**.
 
• Newton's First Law of Motion states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• This law is also known as the law of inertia, where inertia is the resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity.
 
• When the car turns, the passengers inside experience a force due to inertia that makes them feel as if they are being thrown outward.
 
• This outward force is actually the inertia of the passengers trying to keep them moving in a straight line while the car changes direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Law of Motion**

 
 
• This law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.
 
• It is expressed by the equation F=ma" id="MathJax-Element-51-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-39-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-15-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-123-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-137-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-32-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-65-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-43-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma" id="MathJax-Element-5-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">F=maF=ma
 F=ma
 F=ma F=ma F=ma F=ma F=ma F=ma F=ma F = ma , where F is the net force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Third Law of Motion**
 
 
• This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• This means that forces always come in pairs; if one object exerts a force on another, the second object exerts a force of equal magnitude but in the opposite direction on the first object.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Momentum**
 
 
• This principle states that the total momentum of a closed system is conserved if no external forces are acting on it.

questions.question: When the force and the displacement are in the same direction, then work done will be:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**positive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the **force** and **displacement** are in the same direction, the **angle between force and displacement** is **0 degrees**.
 
• The mathematical expression for **work done** is given as: **Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• When θ = 0°, the value of **cos(θ) = 1**, so the formula simplifies to: **W = F × d × 1 = F × d.**
 
• Since both force and displacement are in the same direction, their magnitudes are **positive**, leading to a **positive value for work done**.
 
• This signifies that the energy is being **transferred to the object**, causing displacement in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Examples include pushing a box forward or lifting an object upwards, where the displacement occurs in the same direction as the applied force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero**__

 __
 
• If the angle between force and displacement is **90 degrees**, then the **cos(90°) = 0**, resulting in **zero work done**.
 
• This happens when the force does not contribute to the displacement, such as carrying an object horizontally without vertical displacement.
 
 
 
• **Negative**__
 __
 
• If the force and displacement are in **opposite directions**, the angle θ = 180°, and **cos(180°) = -1**, leading to **negative work done**.
 
• Negative work is observed when a force opposes the motion, such as friction slowing down a moving object.
 
 
 
• **Either Positive or Negative**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the work done depends on the **specific relationship** between the force and displacement directions.
 
• It cannot be both positive and negative at the same time; it depends on the angle θ.
